subject: Avery Systems renewal: conditional rate lock & volume incentive
messages:
From: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@averysys.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal pricing and rate lock request

Hi Laura,

We're kicking off renewal planning for Avery Systems (term ends 2028-05-31). Our procurement team is asking whether Redwood can offer a short-term rate lock while we finalize internal budgets — ideally a 12-month price hold on our current committed rates and an additional volume incentive for any uplift above 20% of our current commit.

High level:
- Current commit: 1.2M tokens/month (reserved)
- Expected growth: forecasting 30-50% next 12 months with new product launches
- Ask: 12-month rate lock, a stepped volume discount (2 tiers), and consideration of a one-time onboarding credit to offset Q3 burst spend.

Can you share a proposal or an outline of concessions you can consider? Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Cloud Procurement
Avery Systems

[attachment: usage_report_q4.csv]
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@averysys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and rate lock request

Thanks Daniel — great to hear from you and congrats on the product launches. I've attached the Q4 usage export you referenced so our numbers line up (usage_report_q4.csv).

We can absolutely support a rate ceiling and a volume-incentive structure. To move quickly, here's a provisional option we can run past legal and finance:

Provisional offer (subject to final SOW/addendum):
- 6-month unconditional rate lock at current committed unit price, followed by an optional 12-month extension conditional on hitting volume milestones
- Volume incentive: +10% price credit when monthly usage exceeds 120% of committed baseline; +18% credit when usage exceeds 150% baseline (applied as monthly bill credits)
- One-time onboarding credit: $35k applied against Q3 overage (if uplift occurs before 2028-09-30)
- Commitment flexibility: allow up to +30% burst capacity with tiered overage pricing during first 3 months of renewal to smooth migration

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Avery prefers a 6-month provisional + conditional extension vs a straight 12-month locked rate (we can model economics both ways).
2) If conceptually OK, Marissa and I will draft the commercial addendum and loop Markus for redlines.
3) We can align on a DocuSign workflow for signatures once commercial terms agreed.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to walk through the milestones and invoicing mechanics?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0184

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Avery renewal concession recommendation

Internal note — Laura / Markus,

Avery is strategic for our platform benchmarks and a good reference for finance. My quick take: push for a 12-month rate lock but gate the extension on quarterly volume milestones (so their commitment is explicit and we protect unit economics). If we give a one-time $35k onboarding credit, require it to be tied to an executed PO that references the addendum.

Suggested changes to Laura's provisional:
- Make the initial lock 12 months (not 6), but include a performance escape clause at month 6 if utilization < 80% of baseline (protects us).
- Convert the +10% / +18% credits to usage rebates applied quarterly (simpler to invoice).
- Require a mutual cadence: monthly usage reports + a single quarterly reconciliation.

I'll prepare a commercial addendum draft for Markus to review.

-Marissa
Sr. Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Laura / Marissa,

Thanks — tagging legal comments. We can accept a 12-month rate lock with the following contract-level controls:
- Performance escape at month 6 if utilization < 80% of baseline (consistent with Marissa's suggestion)
- Quarterly reconciliation and rebate mechanics referenced in the addendum (we will not be invoicing monthly credits; rebates will be processed after reconciliation)
- PO requirement: onboarding credit payable only if PO references the addendum and billing instructions are provided

I've attached a redline of the Master Agreement + addendum template with placeholders for milestone percentages and rebate calculations (Avery_Systems_MA-AL_v2-redlines.pdf). Please review and I'll prepare a clean DocuSign packet once wording is final.

-Markus Klein
VP, Legal Operations (Contracting), Redwood Inference

Daniel — thanks for the quick collaboration. Summary of the path we discussed and proposed next steps: 

Agreed commercial path (draft):
- 12-month rate ceiling at current committed unit price with a performance escape at month 6 if utilization < 80% baseline.
- Quarterly volume rebates: +10% rebate when quarterly usage > 120% baseline; +18% rebate when quarterly usage > 150% baseline. Rebates calculated on the overage portion and applied post-reconciliation.
- One-time $35k onboarding credit payable against Q3 overage, conditional on an executed PO that references the addendum and net-30 payment terms.
- Operational: monthly usage exports shared by Avery; quarterly reconciliation call.

Next steps:
1) I'll send the addendum redline to your procurement team for an initial review (Markus attached a redline).
2) If acceptable, we'll package a DocuSign packet and route it to your signatory. DocuSign link will be shared here: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/abc123def
3) Please share the PO (or PO number) referencing the addendum so we can apply the onboarding credit.

Would you like to confirm the 30-min slot tomorrow at 10:00am PT? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting this locked in.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
